original_question: For a bipartite planar graph, choose any Kasteleyn matrix K obtained from the bipartite adjacency matrix by changing signs so that all non-zero determinant contributions have the same sign. Determine the combinatorial significance of the spectrum of KK*, which is independent of the particular Kasteleyn signing.
target_in_paper: Problem 6 in Section 2 (Lozenges): What is the significance of the spectrum of KK*, where K is any Kasteleyn-Percus matrix associated with a bipartite planar graph? ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/eom.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target very closely: it is about a bipartite planar graph, a Kasteleyn-type signing of the bipartite adjacency matrix, the fact that the choice of signing is not canonical, the invariance of the spectrum of KK* under that choice, and the request for a combinatorial meaning of that spectrum. Those are exactly the cues used to motivate Problem 6. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/eom.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's term is Kasteleyn-Percus matrix, not just Kasteleyn matrix. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/eom.pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, K should be identified as the signed bipartite adjacency matrix: rows indexed by white vertices, columns by black vertices, with entry 0 for nonadjacent pairs and +/-1 for adjacent pairs. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/eom.pdf))
The official problem is phrased for a bipartite planar graph in general, not just for honeycomb graphs or hexagons. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/eom.pdf))
K* should be identified as the adjoint of K, so the spectrum under discussion is the eigenvalue multiset of the square matrix KK*. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/eom.pdf))

Your determinant-based description of the signing is slightly narrower than the paper's formulation; if one keeps that description, one should explicitly say one is restricting to the balanced/square case, whereas the paper simply speaks of any Kasteleyn-Percus matrix associated with the graph. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/eom.pdf))

The paper asks for the significance of the spectrum; it does not narrow this to computing the spectrum, its determinant, or a product formula. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/eom.pdf))
refined_question: For a bipartite planar graph G with a fixed black/white bipartition, let K be any Kasteleyn-Percus matrix of G, meaning the signed bipartite adjacency matrix whose rows correspond to white vertices, whose columns correspond to black vertices, and whose nonzero entries are +/-1 on adjacent white-black pairs. Writing K* for the adjoint of K, the paper notes that although the choice of K is not canonical, the spectrum of KK* is independent of that choice. What combinatorial significance does this spectrum have?
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 6, not the neighboring cokernel question (Problem 5) and not the later determinant-of-KK* questions (Problems 26-27). The decisive match is the immediately preceding context: Propp explains that K is not canonically defined because one may modify signs in the bipartite adjacency matrix in different ways, then states that the spectrum of KK* is nevertheless independent of the chosen Kasteleyn-Percus matrix, and then asks exactly for the significance of that spectrum. I therefore kept the scope at arbitrary bipartite planar graphs and preserved the paper's open-ended formulation instead of broadening it into a stronger or different problem. The progress note mentions Nicolau Saldanha's proposed interpretation, but the nearest official formulation in the paper is still Problem 6 itself. ([faculty.uml.edu](https://faculty.uml.edu/jpropp/eom.pdf))
